Vodafone Lifts FY27 Guidance as German Slide and €4.85 Billion Impairment Test the Story
sum: Vodafone has raised its outlook for the 2027 financial year, projecting adjusted operating profit after lease costs (EBITDAaL) of EUR 13.2 to 13.4 billion. The group also lifted its adjusted free cash flow target to EUR 2.8 to 3.0 billion. Investors, however, greeted the upgrade coolly: the stock was down 1.8% on the day.

The improved guidance rests on first-half momentum. For the six months of FY27, Vodafone posted adjusted EBITDAaL of EUR 6.5 billion, an organic gain of 6.4%. Group service revenue reached EUR 18.4 billion, up 5.8% on an organic basis, while total revenue climbed 11.4% to EUR 21.9 billion.

Reported profit tells a different story. Vodafone booked a net loss of EUR 3.6 billion for the half, dragged down by a EUR 4.85 billion impairment on its German business and a EUR 2.2 billion write-down on active deferred tax assets in the UK. Those charges sit alongside the raised operating and cash flow targets, sharpening the contrast between the underlying trend and the balance sheet hit.
Shareholders are nonetheless getting more: the interim dividend rises 2.5% to 2.306 eurocents per share.

The decisive variable for the upgraded targets is Germany, where organic service revenue slipped 0.5% after previously growing 1.2%, according to Reuters. Enterprise customers and Africa delivered stronger performances, and the question for investors is whether those businesses can keep offsetting the German drag.

Vodafone is moving to shore up the unit. First-half gross savings came to EUR 200 million, including the elimination of 3,000 positions. The German division intends to simplify its structures and lean more heavily on artificial intelligence, with investment also directed toward IT, fibre networks and digital services, as it looks to sharpen its competitive edge.

The direction of German service revenue matters more than group growth in isolation. Stabilisation there would remove a major burden; a deepening decline would force the other divisions to carry more of the load. Analysts and investors will therefore be tracking the German figures and the resilience of growth elsewhere together at each reporting date.

sum: Vodafone Share Price Analysis: Rises 0.39%, Testing Support Level
Technical analysis of Vodafone stock on November 9, 2026: price 116.95 GBp, trend downtrend, RSI 43.6, support 116.50, resistance 122.05.

Vodafone Group shares closed at 116.95 pence on the London Stock Exchange on Monday, November 9, 2026, up 0.39% from the previous close of 116.50. The move was small. Yet it is the kind of bounce that technical analysts watch closely in a downtrend: the shares rose toward their 20-day average without reaching it, and that pattern is the one bearish signal in the day's screen, with no bullish counterpart.

The trend is down. The stock trades below both its 20-day average of 118.64 and its 50-day average of 122.78, and the 20-day line sits under the 50-day line. A moving average is simply the mean closing price over a set number of sessions, so shares below both lines are being priced lower than their recent history. The 20-day average itself fell 0.88% over five days. There was no new crossover between the two averages on the latest session. The bearish alignment is already established rather than freshly formed.

Over longer windows the price has barely moved: a 0.09% gain over five days and a 0.21% change over one month. A stock that has gone nowhere in a month while sitting under falling averages is stuck rather than recovering. The 3-month range runs from a high of 132.07 to a low of 114.30, and the latest close sits at roughly 8% of the 20-day range. That puts it near the bottom of recent trading, just above the 20-day support at 116.50.

As shown in the chart, price is pressed against the lower half of the Bollinger Bands, the envelope drawn two standard deviations around the 20-day average. The bands sit at 121.70 (upper), 118.64 (middle) and 115.58 (lower), and the close registers a %B reading of 22%. In plain terms, the price is in the lower quarter of its normal statistical range.

Momentum indicators do not confirm the downtrend with conviction. The 14-day Relative Strength Index, which measures the pace of recent gains against losses on a 0–100 scale, stands at 43.6. That is neutral, below the midpoint but well clear of the 30 level that usually marks oversold conditions.

sum: Trending Stocks Today, November 9, 2026: PC Jeweller, Vodafone Idea, YES Bank, Empower India Among Top NSE Traded Shares

Mumbai, November 9: Shares of PC Jeweller, Vodafone Idea, YES Bank and Empower India were the most actively traded stocks on the National Stock Exchange (NSE) on Monday, November 9. PC Jeweller declined 2.53%, while Vodafone Idea fell 1.95% and YES Bank shed 1.50%. Empower India was the biggest loser among the four, dropping 4.96%, as investors tracked company-specific developments and recent price movements.

PC Jeweller shares declined on Monday after Diwali on Sunday. Along with jewellery stocks, it had attracted buying interest on Friday which is Dhanteras. The stock had gained as investors positioned themselves for stronger festive-season purchases of gold, silver and other precious metals. PC Jeweller has risen 2% over the past five trading sessions and 4.2% over the past month.

Investors are now looking for evidence that festive-season demand will translate into higher sales volumes and stronger earnings for organised jewellery retailers. The December quarter is a crucial period for the sector, as Dhanteras, Diwali and the subsequent wedding season typically account for a significant portion of annual jewellery purchases.

Dhanteras, also known as Dhantrayodashi, marked the beginning of the Diwali festivities. Buying gold, silver, jewellery, coins and other valuables on the occasion is considered auspicious in India, making it one of the biggest annual demand drivers for jewellery retailers.

Vodafone Idea shares declined on Monday despite further progress in the telecom operator’s proposed Rs 35,000-crore debt financing from a consortium led by State Bank of India (SBI). According to an ETBFSI report, SBI has approved the loan proposal and circulated its appraisal to other participating lenders, taking the funding arrangement a step closer to finalisation.

The National Bank for Financing Infrastructure and Development (NaBFID) is expected to approve an exposure of Rs 4,000 crore shortly, while Punjab National Bank (PNB) is likely to decide on its participation within the next 10 days. Union Bank of India is expected to take a call by the end of November. The individual exposure of these lenders is yet to be finalised.

The share price weakness comes despite an improvement in the company’s recent financial performance and its announcement earlier in October that it had settled its outstanding debt with a consortium of 14 banks.

Here’s my top FTSE 100 telecoms stock (and it’s not Vodafone or BT)
sum: Airtel Africa (LSE:AAF) might not be the most famous name on the FTSE 100, but its share price performance over the past five years has been nothing short of remarkable.

Since October 2021, the telecoms group has seen its market-cap nearly treble. It's the sort of result that would make shareholders in BT and Vodafone, another two Footsie stocks in the sector, extremely jealous. But I don't think the party's over yet…

In October, the company separately listed its money division, formally known as Airtel Mobile Commerce. It provides a financial services platform that enables users to send, receive, and store money directly on their mobile phones without needing a traditional bank account. In rural Africa, it's been a real game changer.

Airtel Africa retains a 77.85% interest in the business, which currently (2 November) has a market-cap of £5.08bn. Airtel Africa itself is valued at £9.94bn. This is very close to the group's pre-separation valuation. In other words, spinning out its money business has had no impact. Not yet, anyway.

However, looking ahead, I think it could be a smart move. Historically, telecoms companies have attracted lower valuations than other sectors. But Airtel Money is more akin to a rapidly-growing technology company. Indeed, its first set of results as a standalone entity were impressive.
During the six months to 30 September, customer numbers increased 18.7% to 56.7m. And compared to the same period a year earlier, revenue was 34% higher. Basic earnings per share (EPS) jumped 21.1%.
Additionally, the company declared its first dividend and is aiming to return a massive 80% of earnings to shareholders each year. Of course, payouts are never guaranteed.

Vodafone Shares Fall 3.7% Following SpaceX Spectrum Deal and VodafoneThree Investor Briefing
sum: Vodafone Group (LSE:VOD) shares declined 3.7% to 119.75 pence on Friday, as investors assessed developments in the telecommunications sector and updated financial targets announced at the company's VodafoneThree Investor Briefing.

The decline followed news that SpaceX had agreed to acquire a portfolio of low-band wireless spectrum in the United States, a development that has drawn attention to potential changes in competition between satellite communications providers and established mobile network operators.

The transaction has raised questions about the longer-term competitive implications of satellite-based connectivity services for traditional telecommunications businesses, although the direct financial impact on Vodafone remains uncertain.
Vodafone shares also came under pressure following Thursday's investor briefing, during which the company outlined revised financial and operational objectives for its merged UK mobile business.

The company increased its annual cost savings target for VodafoneThree to £1 billion by the financial year ending 2032, compared with its previous objective of £700 million by the financial year ending 2030.
Vodafone also introduced a target for adjusted earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation after leases (EBITDAaL) to grow at a mid-to-high single-digit annual rate through FY2032.
The revised objectives reflect the company's plans to deliver additional efficiencies and improve profitability following the combination of Vodafone's UK operations with Three.

sum: First-quarter revenue rose 9.7% to €10.3bn, with growth boosted by the addition of Three UK revenue. Organic Service revenue growth was 5.2% to €8.6bn, with all segments contributing positively.
Adjusted cash profit (EBITDAaL) rose 6.2% organically to €2.9bn, with margins up 0.6 percentage points to 28.5%.

Full-year guidance has been updated to include nine months of Safaricom following completion of the transaction. Vodafone now expects adjusted cash profit of €13.0-13.3bn and free cash flow of €2.6-2.9bn, with performance expected at the upper end of both ranges.

Vodafone’s first quarter was another step in the right direction. Growth was broad-based, and there’s new guidance that suggests upgrades to consensus. The turnaround is gaining credibility, but there’s still work to be done.

Sales in the telecom sector should be relatively robust, as broadband and mobile services are hardly optional. Yet, over the last decade, telecom giants have had to pump huge sums of cash into building out fibre networks and snapping up parts of the 5G spectrum. The main challenge has been the low sales growth relative to spending in telecoms compared to other sectors.

In response to several years of underperformance, Vodafone has evolved its strategy. There have been job cuts, the merger of its UK business with Three UK, and sales of the underperforming Spanish and Italian divisions.

Vodafone also plans to buy the remaining 49% stake in VodafoneThree. The original agreement included an option to acquire the stake after three years, so moving after just one year suggests confidence in the early integration progress. Owning the whole business should make it easier to move quickly and capture the planned benefits, but it also increases Vodafone’s financial exposure if delivery falls short.

Investors are speculating about whether his stake could act as a catalyst for further strategic moves, including potential consolidation opportunities or accelerated execution of Vodafone's existing restructuring plans across its European footprint.

Vodafone has spent recent periods executing a wide-ranging turnaround strategy, including divesting non-core assets, simplifying its corporate structure and focusing capital on its strongest markets. sum: Vodafone (VOD.UK) shares jumped more than 11% on Friday after one of the largest transactions in the European telecommunications sector in recent years was announced. Vega, an investment vehicle controlled by the family of French telecom billionaire Xavier Niel, agreed to acquire Emirates Telecommunications Group's (e&) entire 16.2% stake in Vodafone for approximately £4.4 billion (€5.1 billion / around $6 billion).

At first glance, the market's reaction appeared to be driven simply by the acquisition price. However, investors saw much more than just a premium over Vodafone's previous share price. For many market participants, the transaction represents a strong vote of confidence from one of Europe's most experienced telecom investors, suggesting that Vodafone still has considerable untapped value.
Following regulatory approvals, Vega will become Vodafone's largest shareholder, replacing e&, which is exiting its investment entirely.

Importantly, Xavier Niel emphasized that he has no intention of acquiring the entire company. Under the UK Takeover Code, Vega has confirmed that the investment is intended to be a long-term strategic minority holding designed to support Vodafone's future development rather than gain control of the business.

That distinction matters. Markets typically view short-term financial investors very differently from strategic industry specialists with decades of operational experience. In this case, Vodafone is gaining a shareholder that has successfully built and developed some of Europe's largest telecommunications businesses.
The purchase price suggests Vodafone may have been undervalued
The shares were purchased at approximately 110.5 pence per share, in addition to Vodafone's final dividend.

Vodafone Idea may sell the said shares to pay government dues at later stage and incur capex to drive growth, the report suggested.

The move is expected to strengthen Vodafone Idea’s balance sheet and support its ongoing debt-raising efforts. Following the Bloomberg report, Vodafone Idea shares soared 9.68 per cent to hit a high of Rs 12.34 apiece, taking its one-month rise to 34 per cent.

Vodafone Idea shares have been in focus recently after a few brokerages turned positive on the telecom operator following the reassessment of its Adjusted Gross Revenue (AGR) dues, which were reduced to Rs 64,046 crore from Rs 87,695 crore. Analysts said the AGR relief could improve the company’s fundraising prospects, while adding that a tariff hike remained the key catalyst for the telecom stock.

sum: Most traded stocks today: Frontline indices, the Sensex and the Nifty 50, clocked strong gains during the session as hopes prevailed that the US and Iran would resolve their conflict, which would drive crude oil prices lower and reduce inflationary risks from the global economy.

According to reports, US President Donald Trump signalled that the ceasefire between the US and Iran may not be extended. Meanwhile, reports also suggested that Vice President JD Vance is expected to depart for Islamabad by 21 April morning to resume negotiations with Iran, as Iran is reportedly considering attending peace talks with the US.

The 30-share pack Sensex jumped over 700 points, or nearly 1%, during the session to the level of 79,234, while the NSE counterpart Nifty 50 hit an intraday high of 24,561, rising nearly 200 points, or 1%.

Meanwhile, Vodafone Idea, Billionbrains Garage Ventures (Groww), Bank of Maharashtra, Lemon Tree Hotels, Ola Electric Mobility, Suzlon Energy, YES Bank, Reliance Power, Jaiprakash Power Ventures (JP Power), and Adani Power were among the most traded stocks, or most active stocks in terms of volume, on the NSE in Tuesday's session.

Hindustan Construction Company (HCC), STL Networks, Tata Gold Exchange Traded Fund, PC Jeweller, Rolex Rings, Vedanta, GTL Infrastructure, HFCL, Jio Financial Services, and PNB Housing Finance were also among the most traded stocks on the NSE.

Vodafone Idea: More than 19 crore shares changed hands as the stock rose nearly 3% during the session, a day after falling 1.5%, snapping its three-day winning run. Vodafone Idea shares have gained more than 13% so far in April after falling more than 19% in March. Vodafone Idea said in an exchange filing on 17 April that the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) imposed a financial penalty of ₹21.46 lakh on it. The company said it was reviewing the order and evaluating the next steps in this matter.

Billionbrains Garage Ventures (Groww): Over 14 crore shares changed hands as the stock surged nearly 9% during the session, looking set to snap its three-day losing streak. Shares of the company jumped a day after it announced a 122% year-on-year jump in its consolidated net profit to ₹686 crore for Q4FY26. So far in April, the stock has surged 40%

Vodafone (Q3 Update): weak revenue, full-year guidance maintained
sum: Vodafone reported third-quarter organic revenue growth of 3.0% to €10.5bn. Within that, Service revenue grew by 5.4% to €8.5bn, marking a slowdown from the prior quarter as UK growth slipped into negative territory.
€3.5bn of its €4.0bn share buyback programme is complete, with the final €500mn tranche commencing today.
Full-year guidance was reiterated, with underlying cash profit and free cash flow expected to land at the upper end of their €11.3-11.6bn and €2.4-2.6bn target ranges respectively.

Vodafone’s third-quarter revenue came in a touch below market forecasts as the UK slipped into negative growth, spooking markets on the day. But momentum continued in its largest region, Germany, helping to keep full-year profit guidance on track.

Sales in the telecom sector should be relatively robust, as broadband and mobile services are hardly optional. Yet, over the last decade, telecom giants have had to pump huge sums of cash into building out fibre networks and snapping up parts of the 5G spectrum. The main challenge has been the low sales growth relative to spending when you look at telecoms compared to other sectors.

In response to several years of underperformance, Vodafone has an evolved strategy. There are job cuts, the merger of its UK business with Three UK (now complete), and sales of the underperforming Spanish and Italian divisions.

Germany remains Vodafone’s toughest nut to crack. After hefty investment, the market has been slow to deliver, and execution missteps in recent years have compounded the challenge. Regulatory changes and last year’s price hikes left Vodafone on the back foot. Now, service revenue in the region has squeezed out a sliver of growth for the second quarter in a row. But sustained and improved growth will be the real test.

Vodafone Idea Loss Narrows to ₹5,524 Crore; Shares Gain 6%
sum: - Vodafone Idea (Vi) reported a narrower net loss of ₹5,524 crore for the September quarter, down from ₹6,608 crore in the previous quarter.
- Motilal Oswal attributed the improvement to a 26% drop in interest costs and a one-time settlement with a vendor, likely Indus Towers.
- Vi shares rose 5.78% in early trade on Tuesday to ₹10.06 on the BSE.

Vodafone Idea (Vi) on Monday reported a narrower net loss for the quarter ended September 30 at ₹5,524 crore, compared to ₹6,608 crore in the previous quarter. According to Motilal Oswal, the decline was primarily due to a 26% quarter-on-quarter drop in interest costs and a one-time settlement with a vendor.

The brokerage believes the vendor in question is Indus Towers. Vi shares were up 5.78% in early trading on Tuesday, reaching ₹10.06 on the BSE at 9:48 am. Meanwhile, Indus Tower's shares were up 0.33% to ₹399.80.

In Q2 FY26, Vodafone Idea’s revenue stood at ₹11,200 crore, up 1.6% quarter-on-quarter and 2% year-on-year. The company reported an EBITDA of ₹4,690 crore, an increase of 1.6% QoQ and 3% YoY—about 2% higher than estimates—driven by better revenue and lower network costs. The EBITDA margin remained stable at 41.8%, improving by 25 basis points from last year.

Vodafone Idea’s average revenue per user (ARPU) rose 1.2% quarter-on-quarter to ₹167, a 7% increase from last year and slightly above estimates. The growth was attributed to an extra day in the quarter and an improved subscriber mix. Customer ARPU, excluding machine-to-machine (M2M) connections, rose 1.6% to ₹180. The company’s total subscriber base stood at 19.67 crore, down by 10 lakh from the previous quarter, in line with expectations. Monthly churn inched up to 4.3%, indicating more users switching networks.
